run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Observed: the payment-api application in namespace app-100a (pod_name label payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-4k9ng) began failing at 13:49:24Z with ConnectionPoolExhausted / 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' (pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 7-37, wait_time_ms 5216-23444) and logged /healthz 503 'Health check failed - database unreachable' at 13:57:29Z and 14:01:50Z; error counts per 5-minute window stayed non-zero from 13:49:48Z through 14:49:18Z. The same log stream shows its own database query latency (DEBUG 'Database query executed', duration_ms) at a 15-88 ms p90 baseline from 12:30:42Z to 13:39:18Z, then 1252 ms in the window ending 13:51:12Z and 2355-4953 ms through 14:48:36Z, with completed DB query volume unchanged at 1-2 per 5 minutes, so the failure is a latency-driven connection-pool exhaustion inside payment-api, not evidence of a request surge. What the database dependency actually did in that window is not observable here: Loki returned no app-219 log streams, Prometheus and Jaeger answered SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call, and the DB endpoint/pool settings live in Secrets that cannot be read. The only database workload in the cluster is Deployment mariadb in namespace app-219 (service mariadb:3306), which is therefore the leading candidate dependency, but its own state during 13:45 is unverified and no fault-injection setting was found switched on. Current Kubernetes objects were created at 18:25-18:27Z, after the incident, so they do not describe the incident-time objects.

claims.text: The payment-api pod in app-100a (log label pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-4k9ng) logged repeated 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001, stack 'at PaymentService.processPayment() / at DatabasePool.acquire()') and 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 7-37 and wait_time_ms 5216-23444, from 13:49:24Z to 14:28:27Z.

The same payment-api log stream records /healthz returning status_code 503 with message 'Health check failed - database unreachable' at 13:57:29Z (response_time_ms 5009) and 14:01:50Z (response_time_ms 9684).

The earliest matching error line for namespace app-100a in a query covering 12:00Z-13:50Z was the 13:49:24Z pool-exhausted error (that query returned exactly one line), and the Loki error-count series for app-100a is non-zero in every 5-minute window from 13:49:48Z through 14:49:18Z.

The p90 of the payment-api DEBUG 'Database query executed' duration_ms (5-minute quantile over {namespace="app-100a", job="payment-api"}) was 15-88 ms in the sampled windows from 12:30:42Z to 13:39:18Z, then 1252 ms in the window ending 13:51:12Z, and 2355-4953 ms in sampled windows through 14:48:36Z - a same-measurement comparison against the pre-13:45 baseline.

Individual DEBUG query records support the same shift: duration_ms 65 with 44 rows at 13:34:45Z, duration_ms 1252 with 98 rows at 13:50:55Z, and duration_ms 3106 with 70 rows at 14:28:27Z, for the same statement 'SELECT * FROM payments WHERE status = ?'.

A request-volume surge is not supported: the count of completed 'Database query executed' lines per 5 minutes stayed at 1-2 for every sampled window from 12:30:42Z to 14:48:36Z, so the latency rise occurred without more completed DB work being logged.

Deployment payment-api-100a in app-100a runs a single container named payment-api from image python:3.9-slim with command ['python','/app/app-direct-push.py'], memory limit 256Mi, cpu request 10m, an liveness probe on /healthz:8080 and the application script mounted from Secret payment-api-100a-script; its single ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 and pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-4k9ng were created at 2026-11-23T18:25:48Z, i.e. after the 13:45 incident, so these objects are not the incident-time objects.

The only database workload present in the cluster besides otel-demo's valkey-cart is Deployment mariadb in namespace app-219 (image mariadb:11.6.2, container env from Secret mariadb-secret, container port 3306), exposed by Service mariadb port 3306 whose endpoint is pod mariadb-54b58cdd6d-dknwd:3306; no PersistentVolumeClaims exist in the cluster.

All 20 retained Kubernetes events lie between 2026-11-23T18:25:26Z and 18:25:58Z and describe pod creation/startup plus two Endpoints Warning 'FailedToCreateEndpoint' (loki at 18:19:52Z/18:25:26Z, mariadb at 18:25:57Z); no event covers the 13:45Z incident window, and the Endpoints warnings coincide with the late environment build, not with the payment-api errors.

A Loki query for log volume by namespace over 12:00Z-15:00Z with selector {namespace=~".+"} returned only one series, namespace app-100a, so no other namespace's logs (including app-219) were returned for that interval.

Mechanism: a slowdown of the database dependency that payment-api uses (query duration rising from a 15-88 ms baseline to 1.2-5 s from roughly 13:45-13:51) held all 20 pooled connections, so incoming requests waited up to ~23 s and failed with ConnectionPoolExhausted, and the DB-backed /healthz probe answered 503 'database unreachable'; the pool limit of 20 is the amplifier, not the trigger.

The slowed dependency is most plausibly Deployment mariadb in namespace app-219 (service mariadb:3306), the only database workload in the cluster, but this is unverified: no app-219 logs were returned for the incident window, no Prometheus or Jaeger data was reachable, and the DB endpoint/pool configuration sits in Secrets (payment-api-100a-script, mariadb-secret) that cannot be read.

Fault-injection feature flags were considered and not adopted: the only readable fault-style settings are the flags in ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo), including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, and every flag there has defaultVariant 'off' and targets otel-demo services rather than the app-100a payment-api; this is the configmap's post-incident state, so its 13:45 values remain unknown.

Investigate the database tier for 13:45Z directly: MariaDB server-side signals (InnoDB lock waits, slow query log, max_connections, CPU/IO against its 500m CPU / 512Mi memory limits) and the values inside Secret mariadb-secret, plus the DB endpoint and pool size/timeout used by payment-api in Secret payment-api-100a-script.

Add and alert on database query latency and connection-pool saturation metrics for payment-api (pool in-use/waiting, p90 query duration) instead of relying on application logs, and confirm whether the condition persisted after 14:49Z.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every attempt (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_*_duration and kube-state-metrics series (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available, kube_pod_container_info, etc.) provide no evidence for the incident window; any request-rate, error-rate or resource reading is unknown rather than zero.
Jaeger was unreachable (traces_search and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level evidence exists for the payment service or for a payment-api to database call edge.
Log queries for namespace app-219 over 13:00Z-14:30Z returned no lines at all, so the MariaDB server's own logs and errors during the incident are unknown.

The payment-api application script and its DB connection settings live in Secret payment-api-100a-script, and the MariaDB container environment comes from Secret mariadb-secret; Secrets cannot be read, so the DB host, pool size of 20 as configured, and server-side settings such as max_connections could not be verified.

All Kubernetes objects observed (payment-api, loki, mariadb deployments/ReplicaSets/pods) were created at 18:25:26Z-18:27:05Z, after the incident, and only events from 18:25:26Z-18:25:58Z are retained, so incident-time pod status, restarts, container exit reasons and events for app-100a and app-219 are unknown.

No change history integration is available (change_history not integrated), so what changed at about 13:45Z - including whether the database or the payment-api configuration was modified - could not be checked.
Whether the payment-api condition persisted or recovered after 14:49Z is unknown: Loki returned no lines for app-100a after 14:50Z in the queries run, and the query window ended at 18:26Z.

Node-level resource pressure during the incident is unknown: node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure only at query time (18:26Z), with condition transition times of 14:36:05Z, and no node metrics were reachable.
next_steps: Obtain MariaDB server metrics and logs for 13:40-15:00Z (innodb lock waits, slow queries, connections, CPU/IO) to confirm or drop the mariadb/app-219 hypothesis.
Review the contents of Secret payment-api-100a-script and Secret mariadb-secret with the application owner to establish the DB endpoint, pool size, timeouts and server settings.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access for the incident window so error rates, request latency and span-level call edges can be evaluated.
Check the platform change log for any database or payment-api change at about 13:45Z.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
